f2llm.card_note:
## Revision 2026-11-02: `f2llm-v2-0.6b-q4_k-mixed.gguf` supersedes the Q4_K files

The CUDA/CPU audit measured `f2llm-v2-0.6b-q4_k-imatrix.gguf` at cosine 0.78 against the F32 file, below the Q4_K acceptance bar of 0.94 (`-q4_k-imatrix-c2` 0.76, plain `-q4_k` 0.59). They remain here unchanged for reproducibility but are **superseded**. The replacement keeps Q4_K+imatrix (134-text calibration corpus) for most matrices, with `ffn_down` at Q6_K, `attn_v` and the last three blocks (25-27) at Q8_0, and token embeddings at Q8_0. On a 78-text panel (13 audit texts plus 65 held-out German/English/code/query texts), minimum cosine against `codefuse-ai/F2LLM-v2-0.6B` (sentence-transformers, FP32) is about 0.96, versus 0.77 for the superseded file. The imatrix used is `f2llm-v2-0.6b-q4_k-mixed.imatrix`. Evidence: CrispEmbed `tests/results/below-bar/`.

clip.card_note:
## Revision 2026-11-02: `clip-text-base-q4_k-mixed.gguf` supersedes `clip-text-base-q4_k.gguf`

The CUDA/CPU audit measured `clip-text-base-q4_k.gguf` at cosine 0.933 against the F32 file, below the Q4_K bar of 0.94. Part of that gap was a CrispEmbed runtime defect, not the weights: inputs longer than 75 tokens lost their closing EOS on truncation, so pooling read a content token. That is fixed in CrispEmbed (`CRISPEMBED_CLIP_TEXT_KEEP_EOS`, default on). The replacement uses Q4_K+imatrix, with `attn.v` and encoder block 0 at Q8_0 and token embeddings at Q8_0. On a 78-text panel its minimum cosine against `openai/clip-vit-base-patch16` `get_text_features` (CLIPTokenizerFast, FP32) is about 0.988. Older files remain unchanged for reproducibility; `clip-text-base-q4_k.gguf` is superseded. Evidence: CrispEmbed `tests/results/below-bar/`.

bgem3.card_note:
## Revision 2026-11-02: GGUFs with the sparse and ColBERT heads

The earlier files in this repo (`bge-m3.gguf`, `-q8_0`, `-q4_k*`, `-iq4_xs`) were converted in the default (Ollama) layout, which drops BGE-M3's `sparse_linear` and `colbert_linear` heads, so they support dense retrieval only. They remain unchanged. The new files are converted with `--crisp` and keep both heads:

- `bge-m3-heads-f16.gguf`: F16 encoder with the heads in F32.
- `bge-m3-heads-q8_0-mixed.gguf`: Q8_0, with encoder blocks 0-11 in F16.

Uniform Q8_0 keeps dense and sparse output above the bar but flips a few ColBERT token vectors (per-token minimum cosine 0.61). That error comes from the weights; it does not depend on colbert_linear's precision. Keeping the first 12 blocks in F16 brings it back to 0.973. A Q4_K variant with heads did not clear the bar (ColBERT minimum 0.37-0.60) and is not published. The checks used FlagEmbedding `BGEM3FlagModel` (FP32) on a 77-text panel, comparing dense vectors, lexical weights and every ColBERT token. They need CrispEmbed with the matching tokenizer and sparse fixes (`CRISPEMBED_SPM_COLLAPSE_SPACES` and `CRISPEMBED_SPARSE_KEEP_SPECIAL`, both default-correct). Evidence: CrispEmbed `tests/results/below-bar/`.

bgem3-cuda-margin.card_note:
## Revision 2026-11-03: `bge-m3-heads-q8_0-enc0-15-f16.gguf` supersedes `bge-m3-heads-q8_0-mixed.gguf`

`bge-m3-heads-q8_0-mixed.gguf` (Q8_0, encoder blocks 0-11 in F16) clears the Q8_0 bar on CPU (ColBERT minimum token cosine 0.9726 against FlagEmbedding) but not on CUDA: on a Tesla T4 its ColBERT minimum against the CPU F16 reference is 0.9667. It is kept unchanged and marked superseded. The new file keeps encoder blocks 0-15 in F16 (the rest Q8_0, heads F32): ColBERT minimum 0.9911 against FlagEmbedding BGEM3FlagModel (FP32, 77-text panel, portable CPU build) and 0.9922 on CUDA (T4); dense and sparse stay above 0.9995. 763 MiB, against 1599 MiB for `bge-m3-heads-f16.gguf`. Built with crispembed-quantize `q8_0 --tensor-type 'enc.N.*=f16'` for N = 0..15 from a fresh `--crisp` F32 conversion; the bytes reproduce identically on two different hosts. Evidence: CrispEmbed `tests/results/below-bar/`.
